chunks: Ali ibn Isa (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Mujawir, from Ahmad ibn Nasr al-Tahhan, from Abu Basir. He said: I heard from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him):

that Isa, the Spirit of Allah, passed by a people who were making noise and commotion. So he said: What is wrong with these people? It was said: O Spirit of Allah! So-and-so the daughter of so-and-so is being given in marriage to so-and-so the son of so-and-so on this very night of hers. He said: They noise about today and will weep tomorrow. One of them said: Why, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Because their companion will die on this very night of hers.

Those who agreed with his statement said: God has spoken the truth and His Messenger has spoken the truth. The people of hypocrisy said: How close is tomorrow! When they awoke in the morning, they came and found her in her [usual] state — nothing had happened to her. So they said: O Spirit of Allah! Surely, the one whom you informed us yesterday would die has not died! So Isa (peace be upon him) said: God does what He wills. Take us to her.

So they went racing one another until they knocked on the door, and her husband came out. Isa (peace be upon him) said to him: Seek permission for me to see your wife. He said: So he went to her and informed her that the Spirit of Allah and His Word was at the door with a group. He said: She stayed veiled in her curtained area, so he entered upon her and said to her: What did you do last night?

She said: I did not do anything except what I have been doing in the past. A beggar would come to us every Friday eve, and we would give him what would suffice him until the next [Friday]. He came to me this very night of mine, but I was occupied with my affairs and my family was busy. He called out but no one answered him. He called out again and no one answered, until he called out repeatedly. When I heard his calls, I got up, veiled myself, and gave him as we used to give him.

So he said to her: Move away from your sitting place. Then, there was found beneath her clothes a serpent like a tree trunk, biting its own tail. So he (peace be upon him) said: Because of what you did, God has averted this from you.

key_terms.أفعى: Serpent, viper — the deadly snake found beneath her clothes
key_terms.أهل النفاق: People of hypocrisy (munafiqun) — those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly doubt
key_terms.روح الله: Spirit of God (Ruh Allah) — a title for Prophet Jesus (Isa) in Islamic tradition
key_terms.سائل: Beggar, petitioner — one who asks for alms
key_terms.صرف الله: God averted/turned away — divine protection granted due to charitable action
key_terms.ليلة جمعة: Friday eve — considered a blessed time for charity in Islamic tradition
key_terms.مجلبين: Making noise and commotion — specifically the sounds of a wedding celebration

ai.seo_question: What hadith describes how charity on Friday eve saved a woman from a serpent according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narrative from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through Abu Basir, recounts a miracle story attributed to Prophet Isa (Jesus, peace be upon him) in the Islamic tradition. Isa predicted the death of a bride on her wedding night, but the woman was spared because she had maintained her weekly charity to a beggar on Friday eve despite being occupied on that night. The hadith teaches that consistent charity and perseverance in giving even when inconvenient can avert divine decree — illustrating the powerful protective effect of sadaqa (almsgiving) in Shia Islamic ethics. The hypocrites in the story doubted Isa's prophecy, while believers accepted it, demonstrating the contrast between sincere faith and outward affiliation.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. `Isa (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi `Abdullah al-Barqi from his father from Muhammad b. Sinan al-Mujawir from Ahmad b. Nasr al-Talhan from Abi Basir. He said: I heard from Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as):

`Isa the Spirit of Allah passed by a people who were noising about. So, he said: What is wrong with these [people]? It was said: O Spirit of Allah! So-and-so the daughter of so-and-so is being married to so-and-so the son of so-and-so tonight. He said: They will noise about today, and they will weep tomorrow. So, one of them said: Why, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Because your [female] friend will die on this night.

So, some said: Allah has spoken the truth, and His Messenger has spoken the truth. The people of hypocrisy said: How close is tomorrow! When they awoke, they went, and they found that nothing had happened to her. So, they said: O Spirit of Allah! Surely, you informed us yesterday that she will die, but she did not die! So, `Isa (as) said: Allah does what He wishes. Take us to her.

So, they raced to her until they knocked on the door and her husband came out. Then, `Isa (as) said to him: Give me permission to see your wife.  He said: So, he (the husband) went to her and informed her that the Spirit of Allah and His Word was at the door with a group. He said: She is staying in her place. So, he entered her room [instead] and said to her: What did you do last night?

She said: I did not do anything [special] except that which I have done in the past. A beggar would come to us every Friday eve, and we would give him what would suffice him till the next week. He came to me last night, but I was busy with my affairs, and my family was busy. Then, he called out, and no one greeted him. He called out again, and no one answered, so he kept repeating. When I heard his calls, I stood, I veiled myself, and I gave him what I would give him.

So, he said to her: Move away from your sitting place. Then, they found a serpent like a tree trunk under her clothes, with its teeth clenching its tail. So, he (as) said: Because of what you did, Allah spared you from this.
